text: The Patriots' roller coaster continues after dropping to the Chicago Bears 30-24 on Thursday Night Football, with Caleb Williams outdueling Drake Maye in a game that exposed New England's ongoing turnover struggles—one of Mike Vrabel's four pillars of team identity that the squad desperately needs to shore up if they hope to turn things around. On the practice squad front, the team re-signed LB Jose Ramirez while releasing OL Jacob Rizy, and also cleared P Bryce Baringer from the injured reserve list, continuing the roster tinkering that's become routine in recent weeks. The silver lining came courtesy of RB Rhamondre Stevenson, who reached a career high in receiving yards and continues to do the little things right as he approaches his sixth straight 100-carry season, proving that at least one Patriots offensive piece is performing at a consistently high level. Meanwhile, college football's storied Navy-Notre Dame rivalry makes its first-ever appearance at Gillette Stadium, bringing with it deep Patriots connections and a reminder that even in losing weeks, New England's football home hosts some of the sport's most historic traditions.
